title: CLO International Academic Month Issue 4 (Part 2) Teaching Experience of Virtual and Real Interaction in Digital Fashion Courses
description: In a conversation with Professor Ineke Siersema from the Amsterdam Fashion Institute, we explore the teaching experiences of using CLO software in the curriculum, the new skills required for new talents in the industry, and the successful digital transformation case of the academy's partner ATACAC! The future of digital education is just around the corner!

summary: # CLO International Academic Month Issue 4 (Part 2) ## Teaching Experience of Virtual and Real Interaction in Digital Fashion Courses ### Introduction We are so very excited to hear more about your program and how CLO has been used. So, I'm handing it over to you. You can start whenever you are ready. ### Presentation Setup Okay, I start and share my screen. Yes, please. Thank you for having me here. I'm delighted to be here, and I would like to tell you about my work and what our students are creating with CLO3D. ### Engagement with the Audience Hello, everyone. I don't see you, but please ask questions when you have them. At the end of the Q&A, that would be nice. I have a lot to tell, and I can't cover everything in short, so I apologize. ### Presentation Overview My presentation is titled "From Real to Virtual and Vice Versa: Implementing 3D Digital Prototyping in a Fashion Curriculum." This title reflects our journey as we translate our experiences in the real world into the digital space. ### Understanding 3D in Fashion Design When we talk about 3D modeling in a virtual world, there are many aspects that are genuinely part of the digital realm. It's important to distinguish between the physical world and the 3D world. I always emphasize the physical world because it plays a crucial role in the virtual world. ### The 3D Revolution in Fashion Education The 3D revolution began with curriculum developments in the 1990s, where 3D simulation started gaining traction. We launched a pilot program in 2009, despite many being unfamiliar with 3D technology at that time. Our goal was to create a mindset shift regarding what we perceive as real and what is not. ### Early Developments and Challenges Initially, our outcomes in 3D were not accurate enough, and we needed to enhance user-friendliness in the software. Our objective was to create a reality in drape, look and feel, and provide tools that would facilitate creativity. ### Integration of Traditional and Digital Techniques Through combining traditional craftsmanship with innovative digital software, a new generation of designers emerged. The 3D digital revolution has profoundly affected our students and their working methods. ### Research on 3D Simulation Technology I researched the influence of 3D simulation technology on the fashion design process and its implications for education. The traditional design cycle differs significantly from the 3D digital design cycle, leading to higher efficiency and creativity. ### Master’s Program and Industry Collaboration During my master's program, I collaborated on various interdisciplinary projects with industry partners. We conducted a comparative analysis of different 3D software and found that Pro3D was the most intuitive and user-friendly software available. ### The Evolution of 3D Simulation The evolution of 3D simulation technology has led to the first live virtual fashion shows. Students explored how virtual simulation could extend fashion presentations while promoting sustainability in design. ### Notable Projects and Graduates - Amber J. Slaughter, known for her work with The Fabricant, showcased a collection in a 3D environment without producing physical garments. - Zylva Stelava created a collection that adhered to the principle of zero waste. - Ellie-G. Pom, now a designer at ING, rapidly learned CLO3D and produced impressive prototypes. ### Industry Partnerships and Innovation In 2019, I was inspired by Atokak, which redefined traditional design and production processes. They demonstrated a significant reduction in time and waste, emphasizing new business models that are essential for fashion sustainability. ### Student Projects and Experiences Students engaged in various projects, employing digital tools to explore design possibilities. The curriculum emphasized practical experience, encouraging students to learn by doing. Each student mapped their learning process from start to finish, reflecting on their techniques and outcomes. ### Curriculum Developments The Amsterdam Fashion Institute (Amphi) offers a comprehensive program covering fashion design, business, and branding. With an international community of students, we focus on both traditional and innovative methods in fashion education. ### Learning Outcomes and Skills As students progressed through their studies, they developed critical skills necessary for modern fashion industries, including digital literacy and craftsmanship. The curriculum fosters an environment where students can experiment and innovate. ### Conclusion The journey from real to virtual and vice versa illustrates the transformative power of digital technology in fashion education. Our students are not just learning to create but are becoming pioneers in a rapidly evolving industry. Thank you for your attention, and I look forward to your questions.
